item.title: Website mission and start of creating custom AI tools and workflows
item.description:
🎯 Problem Definition: The Mind Behind the Mission

I have a mind full of ideas, energy, and the ability to shift gears quickly — but also one that’s easily pulled in different directions. I can make huge progress in bursts, but when I work alone or lose momentum, projects can quietly slip through the cracks. The isolation of solo work, especially remote, makes it harder. I miss the real-time interaction and co-creation that comes from sharing physical space with someone.

item.title: Deploy a Crew of AI Agents
Single agent vs. multi-agent.
item.description:
Single Agent vs. Multi-Agent: What’s Best for You?

TL;DR

Think of it like hiring people.
Each single agent is like an employee: they have a role, a backstory (skills, experience, personality), and a task they’re responsible for.

You can hire multiple single agents—each with their own focus.
But in a multi-agent system, those people start working together without you needing to be in the middle.

As long as you’re still figuring out who you need and what they should do, start with one or more single agents.
And add memory early—that’s a game-changer in itself.
